blocks.text: The module documentation defines authorization, policy recheck, argument checks, process supervision, environment filtering, output treatment, sandbox modes, and controlled network behavior.
blocks.title: Shell security and lifecycle contract

blocks.text: ToolOutcome carries output, trust, exit status, and local failure code. CallEnv carries caller-only authorization and callbacks, while ShellConfig validates limits, sandbox, network, and warning settings.
blocks.title: Call data and shell configuration

blocks.anchor: def configure_shell(context: Any, config: ShellConfig) -> None:
blocks.text: Configuration is attached to the session context. Helpers choose the effective config, describe unsandboxed warnings, query sandbox availability, warn once, sanitize inherited environment, and locate bash or sh.
blocks.title: Configuration and environment

blocks.text: TerminalSanitizer removes control characters and complete or bounded escape sequences across chunks. _StreamFilter combines incremental UTF-8 decoding with the sanitizer.
blocks.title: Terminal output sanitization

blocks.text: _OutputBuffer retains head and tail bytes with an omission marker and stream-change labels. _Streamer coalesces callback chunks by size/time and disables a callback after it raises.
blocks.title: Bounded output and streaming

blocks.text: The process helpers inspect cancellation and exit without prematurely reaping, terminate groups, normalize statuses, spawn isolated processes, create optional network mounts, and build sandboxed argv.
blocks.title: Process and sandbox helpers

blocks.anchor: def _execute(context: Any, command: str, timeout_s: int, cfg: ShellConfig, cancel: Any,
blocks.text: _execute validates the root and sandbox state, starts the process, pumps both pipes, enforces timeout/cancel and drain windows, kills leftovers, builds the outcome, and logs only status metadata.
blocks.title: Supervised command execution

blocks.text: run_command performs authorization, policy, argument, callback, and config checks before execution and clears proxy labels afterward. bash validates CallEnv and forwards its fields to run_command.
blocks.title: Public authorization entry points

gotchas: Authorization is required even when policy allows.
If a working sandbox was available but its per-command profile cannot be built, the command is refused rather than downgraded.
Unsandboxed mode can retain the user's filesystem privileges despite environment stripping.
how_it_works: Validates shell configuration and call authorization
Builds sanitized environment and sandbox argv
Kills process groups on timeout, cancel, or exit
purpose: This is the bash executor used by the local tool dispatcher. It rechecks authorization and policy, sanitizes the environment, chooses a sandbox and optional controlled network proxy, supervises a process group, strips terminal controls, bounds output, and returns a ToolOutcome.
summary: Authorizes, sandboxes, runs, streams, sanitizes, bounds, and terminates model-proposed shell commands.
